chapter.title: Data Through Pictures
chapter.tagline: Collecting survey responses, organizing with tally marks, and visualizing data in pictographs and bar graphs
chapter.overview: Samaira and Kabir act as roving child TV reporters, asking classmates how many hours they spend watching TV, playing sports, or reading books. Students record frequencies using five-bar tally marks, design pictographs with clear scale keys, and construct vertical bar charts.

sections.title: Tally Marks & Frequency Tables
sections.subtitle: Grouping counts into bunches of 5 for rapid calculation

storyNarrative.dialogue: Four vertical strokes and a diagonal slash makes a bundle of 5 (卌)! Three bundles plus two single strokes equals 17!

concept.heading: The 5-Gate Tally Convention
concept.keyRule: Tally marks group data in sets of 5 (IIII with cross-bar = 5) to prevent miscounting large totals.

sections.title: Pictographs and Bar Charts
sections.subtitle: Communicating insights visually with scales and bars

storyNarrative.dialogue: In our bar chart, the height of each colored bar instantly shows that 28 students love sports while only 12 watch cartoons!

concept.heading: Interpreting Bar Graph Heights
concept.keyRule: Bar heights are proportional to frequency. A labeled vertical axis with an explicit scale allows direct quantitative comparison.
